Subject: Private VPC networking follow-up

Hi Alex —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery and next steps so your infra team can plan: 

What we heard:
- Preferred deployment: Private VPC (you want network isolation + BYO KMS)
- Key requirements: cross-account VPC peering vs PrivateLink, static IP allowlist for outbound traffic, and on-prem connectivity later this year
- ETA: aiming to deploy a staging environment by mid-October

Technical notes / asks for you before the tech deep-dive: 
1) Confirm whether you prefer AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoints) or VPC peering — each has tradeoffs (PrivateLink avoids route table changes and limits surface, peering can be simpler for high-throughput intra-VPC comms).
2) Please share the CIDR ranges you'd like us to peer with or the principal/account for PrivateLink.
3) Do you require IP-based allowlists for Redwood egress, or will FQDN-based allowlisting be acceptable? If IP allowlist is required, we can provide our egress IP set and an architecture diagram.
4) Any compliance constraints (SOC2 evidence requests, logging retention) we should include in the tech call?

I've attached a short checklist and a diagram to help your network team (redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf, networking-diagram.png).

Proposed next step: 30-45m technical call with Carlos and your infra/security folks — are mornings PT next week available?

Thanks,

— Marissa Cole

Hi Alex / Carlos —

Thanks for the answers. A few clarifications from the engineering side (cc'ing our infra lead Dev and SE Sean):

- PrivateLink vs VPC Peering: for your stated constraints (avoid route changes + isolation) PrivateLink is a good fit. It gives you an interface endpoint per service and avoids transitive routing. The tradeoff is a small per-endpoint cost and slightly higher ops for endpoint management. For high-throughput model serving (large batch inference) we can discuss hybrid options (peering for bulk traffic, PrivateLink for control plane).

- Egress/IP allowlisting: we can provide a stable set of egress IPs for the control plane and provisioning traffic. There's also outbound traffic from model-serving workers when using Dedicated pools; for Private deployments egress can stay within your VPC except for control-plane callbacks. I've attached our current egress IP list (redwood-egress-ips.txt). Please note we also recommend allowing *.redwood.ai for TLS validation if your proxy/firewall can allow FQDNs — some customers do both (IPs + FQDNs) to future-proof.

- Ports/protocols: primarily TLS (443) to our control endpoints. For PrivateLink we'll use TCP 443 to the endpoint. If you plan to use telemetry or metrics push we can provide alternate ports but defaults are over 443.

- Certificates: we support mutual TLS on the control plane for Private deployments; if you require mTLS we'll need a contact for cert exchange and a preferred CA.

Next steps: 
1) Carlos to confirm which AWS account/principal will create the PrivateLink endpoint or provide the VPC peering connection info.
2) Schedule 45m technical workshop with your infra + security and our SE/infra engineers (Sean, Dev).
3) We will share a draft network runbook and firewall rule set after the call.

I've attached the egress IPs file for your networking team.

Best,

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-egress-ips.txt
